steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I see. The photograph does indeed show Huck passing an object to Horne. He is a plausible suspect.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Moving forward, I will handle the situation with Huck "discreetly."

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: That will be all for today. Thank you for your cooperation, Mr. ${PlayerName}. You're free to go now.
steps.female_content: That will be all for today. Thank you for your cooperation, Ms. ${PlayerName}. You're free to go now.

steps.content: [Scene Change: Corridor]
You step back into the corridor, drawing a deep breath to steady your nerves after the conversation with Hilda.
The corridor is silent and empty now. Through the window, a gentle rain mists the glass, carrying the sweet, petrichor scent of damp earth into the still air.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Officer ${PlayerName}! How did it go? I hope Hilda didn't give you a hard time.
...It seems you're not alone after all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She just apologized for startling me. It was fine... Where is everyone else?

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: After what happened, no one wanted to stay in the hall. They've all moved to the dining hall in the annex. Here, let me take you there.

options: Were you waiting here for me?
No need, I can find my way there.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Of course I was. I was really worried about you, Officer.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Hilda's room is—gkkt. A place where people tend to lose their heads.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: She calls it "questioning," but let's be honest, it's an interrogation. Rumor has it her closet doesn't hold clothes, but a full set of... professional tools.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Most people are terrified of being summoned there. It's a genuine relief to see you come out in one piece.

steps.speaker: Option
options: You really don't need to act this way with me.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not some high-ranking official. I don't have the kind of power you might think.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Please, don't say that! In my eyes, you're the most capable and reasonable person I've ever met. My admiration is sincere.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Once I'm done here, I'm going to request a transfer from this backwater DisCity. I want to return to the metropoles and apply to join your Mania Countermeasure Center. When the time comes, maybe you could... mention my name?

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: I don't want to be a spy anymore. I want a job where I can be proud of who I am!
The raw sincerity on his face catches you off guard, leaving you almost lost for words.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Like I said, my influence is limited... but I'll remember what you've asked. If I get the chance, I'll put in a word for you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But if you never wanted this life, why become a spy in the first place...?

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Haha... Well, I've always been... unremarkable. To most people, I was practically invisible. Teachers would skip my name during roll call. I was always the one overlooked. For a long time, I thought that was just my lot in life.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Then one day, Mr. Manphist came to our school. And he... he picked me. Can you imagine what that feels like? For someone who's always been invisible to finally be seen? It was incredible. So I followed him to the agent academy and became a spy.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Mr. Manphist said I was a natural. That people just look right through me. I can be practically standing right next to them, eavesdropping, and they'd never know I was there. It let me accomplish things others couldn't.
In your mind, something suddenly clicks into place.
(The three photos flash past.)

<color=#fb9259>I was a natural. That people just look right through me. I can be practically standing right next to them, eavesdropping, and they'd never know I was there. It let me accomplish things others couldn't.</color>
You stare at Edward, frozen. He meets your gaze with a smile.
But it's all wrong. Gone is the humble, meek man from before.
Bam!
A nearby door crashes open. You try to run, but Edward slams into you from behind, driving the air from your lungs as you hit the floor.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Since you've seen through me... I suppose I have no choice left.
Something thin and sharp—a fishing line—whips around your neck. He yanks from behind, and it instantly slices into your flesh.
You thrash, but every movement only tightens the garrote. Your breath comes in ragged, useless gasps. You claw blindly behind you, reaching for Edward's arms, but your strength is already failing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you... the mole...?

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Oh, no. You've got it all wrong. I'm not the mole...
Edward pauses for a single, terrifying moment. Then he pulls harder. You can even hear a soft, sickening crunch in your throat.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: But it told me I could be!
Warmth floods your neck. Blood.
The world grays out, details dissolving into a smear of nothing. Your final, gurgling pleas are a small, pathetic sound, lost against the corridor's chill and the rain's steady, mocking hiss.
Darkness takes you.
ENDING 6
Option B: No need, I can find my way there.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Oh... I see... My apologies, that was overstepping.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Of course, Officer ${PlayerName}. You're welcome to go on ahead...
He retreats half a step, a flicker of disappointment in his eyes, yet his polite smile remains.
But the moment you pass him, a sudden rush of air whips past the back of your head.
(Black Screen)
Thud!

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: ...Tch. Putting on airs, are we? You should have taken the easy way when offered.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Hand you over to those DisCity people, and I'm home free.
Your legs buckle. The ground rushes up to meet you, and as your vision tunnels into nothing, someone grips your ankles, pulling you into a dark, cold corner.
